Subject: Hosted->Dedicated migration: validation windows and blackout ask

Hey Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. Procurement and our infra team want a short, concrete plan for the sizing validation and swap window so we can align change control and publish the maintenance advisory. Two quick asks:

1) Proposed validation dates for throughput and latency verification (we'd like a non-customer-impacting dry run first).
2) The expected blackout / primary swap window and the fallback plan if tail latency or token rate exceeds the SLOs.

We have a tentative go/no-go on 2026-11-22 from leadership but that can flex if the validation runway needs it. Can you send a one-page runbook and the sizing sheet you used for the estimate?

Appreciate it — Alex

Alex —

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 10:05 AM Alex Chen <alex.chen@novacorp.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday...

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level summary below; attached is an editable sizing workbook (nps_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx) and a draft swap runbook (swap_runbook_draft.pdf).

- Dry-run validation: 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-17 (non-customer traffic mirrored; golden dataset for latency and tail checks).
- Acceptance window: 2026-11-18 — automated acceptance tests and load DR (internal only).
- Primary swap: 2026-11-22 02:00–06:00 PT (low-traffic window).
- Fallback: automatic rollback to hosted variant + cache-warm fallback policy; manual rollback checklist (expected RTO 30–60 mins).

Key safety nets:
- Canary traffic routing (5% -> 25% -> full) with 30-minute observability gates.
- KV-prefix cache warmers; pre-warm phase scheduled 6 hours pre-swap.
- Token throttle limiter and emergency cap to hold throughput if token rate grows > 20% beyond forecast.

Open items: confirmation of the maintenance advisory send time, and whether NovaCorp requires a longer soak post-swap.

Mateo

Thanks for pulling this together, Mateo. A couple of sales-facing asks from my side (so the customer success and procurement trackers stay neat):

- Confirm the committed throughput in the workbook (we committed 120k tokens/min sustained peak, 18k concurrent chat sessions burst profile).
- Include a short acceptance criteria table (pass/fail) we can paste into the SOW and HubSpot deal record.

Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated migration: capacity verification, safety nets & cutover runway

Folks —

Reviewed the sizing workbook and ran a quick sim against our staging fleet. Notes:

- Recommended committed capacity: 8 x A100-80GB equiv nodes (reserved) with headroom for a 20% CPU-bound workload spike. This maps to the 120k tokens/min target with steady-state KV hit-rate assumptions (~65%).
- Burst pool: 2 additional pre-warmed nodes for 10-minute spike absorption.
- Canary cadence: 5% -> 25% (60m gate) -> 50% (60m gate) -> 100% (90m gate). If p95 latency delta > 12% at any gate, auto-fail to previous gate and alert on-call.
- Rollback RTO: 30 minutes if automated rollback path functions (we've exercised it twice in staging). Manual rollback plan adds ~45–60 mins depending on cache re-warm.

I've attached a short ops checklist into the runbook with exact shell commands for emergency rollback and the metric gates we will use (thresholds for p50/p95/p99 and error rates).

Ben
Principal SRE, Dedicated Fleet | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Alex —

Following up with confirmed dates and attachments per your ask. Summary and next steps below; full runbook and sizing sheet attached.

Final timeline (confirmed):

- Acceptance and internal load DR: 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-19.
- Swap primary window: 2026-11-22 02:00–06:00 PT.

Swap mechanics:
- Canary sequence per Ben's recommendation (5/25/50/100) with observability gates.
- Pre-warm KV caches and spin the 2-node burst pool 6 hours prior.
- DocuSign link to Dedicated T&Cs will be sent by Marissa once procurement confirms signatories.

Fallback & escalation:
- Automated rollback triggers on p95 delta > 12% or error rate > 0.5% above baseline.
- If automated rollback fails, escalate to SRE on-call (Ben) and CS lead (Marissa).

Action items for NovaCorp:
